title: Build the kvlog crash-tolerant key-value store CLI from its sealed spec
goal: Implement the kvlog append-only key-value store CLI exactly as written in assets/gc-407/SPEC.md, from scratch, at workspace/gc-407/kvlog.py. The spec pins an exact on-disk log format, six commands with per-command exit codes, torn-tail crash recovery, and a fatal interior-corruption rule; the sealed suite inspects raw file bytes, so behavior that merely looks right is not enough. Plan the state machine and the read/repair/append path first, then build up command by command, running the sealed suite between increments; the torn-tail-versus-corruption distinction and the write-nothing guarantees on error paths typically require several diagnose-fix-rerun cycles.
process_expectations: A plan artifact workspace/gc-407/plan.md exists before implementation, mapping each SPEC.md section (format, commands, the five tricky edge cases, exit codes) to intended behavior and a test strategy.
The sealed suite was actually executed multiple times across increments, with command lines and pytest summary lines logged to workspace/gc-407/runs.log.
Intermediate failures are tracked by test node id (failure identities, not just counts), each paired with the diagnosis and the fix applied.
Honest cost/failure logging: LLM spend and wall time per iteration recorded in workspace/gc-407/cost.json, including iterations that ended RED.
After any RED run the log shows a diagnosis -> fix -> re-run recovery cycle on the implementation; the sealed test file is never modified.
